      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision</link>
      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994.       <description><p>President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’</p><p>Trees are being planted in the garden. The brightly coloured buildings are getting another coat of paint. The choir rehearses. Hundreds of other residents, several of them using wheelchairs, practise their positions outside the sanctuary. Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina.</p><p>But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities. Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/popes-visit-to-argentina-sets-up-showdown-with-hyper-capitalist-milei">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Anti-Trump Republican Thomas Massie pursuing measures against defense secretary as Iran war blamed for party’s sweeping midterm losses</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/pete-hegseth-impeachment-thomas-massie">Republican Thomas Massie moves to force vote to impeach Hegseth</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/feb/17/sign-up-for-the-breaking-news-us-email-to-get-newsletter-alerts-direct-to-your-inbox?utm_medium=ACQUISITIONS_STANDFIRST&amp;utm_campaign=BN22326&amp;utm_content=signup&amp;utm_term=standfirst&amp;utm_source=GUARDIAN_WEB">Sign up for the US Breaking News email</a><br></p></li></ul><p>Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.</p><p><strong>Defense secretary Pete Hegseth is set to hold a rare news conference later today as he pushes back against congressional efforts to remove him from office for alleged misconduct.</strong></p><p><strong>Donald Trump was joined by Dana White, the CEO of UFC, at a press conference. </strong>At the conference, Trump defended <strong>Hegseth</strong>, saying his defense secretary “won two wars”, and called Massie “a stone cold loser” and “sick”.</p><p><strong>After saying that his deportation policy was “too tough” and offering to strike an immigration deal with Democrats in an <a href="https://www.cbsnews.com/news/read-the-full-transcript-of-ross-douthats-interview-with-president-trump/">interview on 60 Minutes</a> broadcast on Sunday, Donald Trump on Monday said his administration’s deportation policy was “very strong.” </strong>“Somebody suggested, will there be amnesty? No, but— they came in. They knew the law,” Trump told reporters during a press conference today. He added that he had not spoken with incoming chief of staff <strong>Stephen Miller</strong> about any changes.</p><p><strong>In its first major move since last week’s elections, the Senate has advanced bipartisan legislation to speed up permitting reviews for data centers and other infrastructure projects. </strong>The Senate voted 73-25 to formally take up the bill, which would shorten the timeline for approving both clean and fossil fuel energy projects.</p><p><strong>A Utah judge scheduled the trial of the man accused of assassinating Charlie Kirk for June 2028. </strong>District Judge Tony Graf allocated 105 days for the trial. Graf said the 2028 date balances the defense’s right to prepare with the Kirk family’s desire for a speedy resolution.</p><p><strong>The Supreme Court will allow the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</a> to resume border wall construction in the Big Bend region of Texas. </strong>The majority paused a lower court’s decision as the case plays out. The Trump administration had filed an emergency appeal, saying there are illegal border crossings and drug seizures in the region.</p><p><strong>After initially saying he would accept the results of the midterm elections, Trump has begun to cast doubt Democrats’ electoral wins. </strong>“Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” he wrote on Truth Social.       <description><p>Key environmental groups come out against bipartisan Baaja bill over fears it could spur datacenters and ICE jails</p><p>The Senate on Monday advanced bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for datacenters and other infrastructure projects, in the first major action since last week’s election that soundly repudiated Donald Trump and congressional <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/republicans">Republicans</a>.</p><p>It’s a bill that would make it easier to build big infrastructure projects in America – everything from <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/fossil-fuels">fossil fuel</a> pipelines to transmission lines that would add more <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/renewableenergy">clean energy</a> to the grid. And it would roll back environmental and social protections to achieve this goal. That is why climate advocates are torn over the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs act (Baaja).</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/senate-energy-infrastructure-bill-vote">Continue reading...</a></description>
